title: Write a Prometheus Alert Rule
intro: The monitoring tutorials had you validating and silencing alerts. Now write one: page someone when checkout's error ratio stays above 5% for 10 minutes.

steps.prompt: Write a rules file with one group named 'checkout-alerts' containing one rule: alert 'CheckoutHighErrorRate', whose expr is the ratio of 5xx requests to all requests for service="checkout" over 5 minutes, compared with > 0.05. It must hold for 10m, carry the label severity: page, and have a summary annotation.
steps.hint: Structure: groups (list) → each group has name and rules (list) → each rule has alert, expr, for, labels, annotations. For the expr, reuse the error-ratio query from monitoring-tutorial-003: sum(rate(...{service="checkout",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(...{service="checkout"}[5m])) > 0.05.
steps.solution:
groups:
  - name: checkout-alerts
    rules:
      - alert: CheckoutHighErrorRate
        expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="checkout",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{service="checkout"}[5m])) > 0.05
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: page
        annotations:
          summary: "Checkout error rate above 5% for 10 minutes"
steps.explanation: A symptom-based, ratio-based alert that only pages for sustained problems.
steps.why: Every design choice here prevents a known failure: a RATIO works at any traffic level (a count doesn't), 'for: 10m' ignores brief spikes (see monitoring-incident-003's flapping alert), and 'severity: page' lets Alertmanager route real emergencies to on-call while lower severities go to a ticket queue instead of waking anyone.
